cohort: 16,811 women ≥ 24 weeks' gestational age who delivered between January 2010 and June 2015 at one perinatal center
finding: A standardized oxytocin protocol was associated with a lower postpartum hemorrhage treatment rate for cesarean and vaginal deliveries, but not for operative vaginal deliveries.
mod_finding: The prophylactic effect of the higher dose oxytocin protocol had the strongest benefit with women delivering vaginally.
